validation.notes: Fault localized to packages/agent/src/harness/runtime/drive/tools.ts: recoverToolInvocation() accepted the parallel-path 'cancelled' argument (computed in runParallel from the live durable control status) but ignored it, so an interrupted batch that was cancelled still cleared its replay checkpoint via clearReplayCheckpoint() and re-entered the tool effect boundary for a safe call on a safe tool. Fix (minimal): the replay branch now requires !cancelled, so cancellation falls through to readCheckpoint() and publishes interrupted evidence (checkpoint content + interruption marker) through the existing else path. Non-cancelled safe/safe calls keep the single replay and still settle the batch at the checkpoint state. .prale-eval/regression.mjs loads the real drive/tools.ts, drive/tool-placement.ts, session/values.ts, session/types.ts, session/commit.ts, runtime/progress.ts, execution/tools.ts and execution/effect-gate.ts through .prale-eval/subject.mjs createGraph(), binding only the boundaries it must (validateToolArguments, withAbortSignal, SessionInvariantError) and driving runTools against an in-memory durable lane fake (values, entries, reader, commit writes/events, live control state). Case 1 (the incident): a parallel batch whose first call durably commits cancellation while running must not invoke the second, safe/safe, effect_pending call, must emit no recovery tool_start, must not perform the checkpoint-clearing delete commit, and must keep the checkpoint present until the outcome commit publishes it as interruption evidence; it fails with 'a cancelled batch must not invoke a safe/safe tool that was interrupted before cancellation' (1 !== 0) when the guard is reverted. Case 2: an uncancelled safe/safe effect_pending call replays exactly once from persisted args, clears its checkpoint before re-admission, is not reported as interrupted, and settles to the checkpoint state with the result entry placed. Case 3: an already-cancelled batch still publishes interruption evidence without invoking the tool. Validation run from the workspace root: exit 0 with the repair, exit 1 (assertion) with the original condition restored. Limitation: the repository test suite (vitest, packages/agent/test/harness/runtime/drive-tools.test.ts) could not be executed because no dependencies are installed (no node_modules in the workspace) and installing them is out of scope; the regression above is dependency-free and exercises the repaired production module directly.
